Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem.  
Each recursive call works on a reduced version of the input until it reaches a simple case that can be solved directly, known as the base case.  
When the base case is reached, the function stops calling itself and the results from each level of recursion are combined as the calls unwind.  
This approach lets complex problems be broken down into easier, repeatable steps, making the code more concise and often easier to understand.
